newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama free-trade zone exports up 5.1 pct in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Panama free-trade zone exports up 5.1 pct in Q1.

text.p: Panama's free-trade zone exports increased 5.1 percent during the first quarter of 1997 compared with the same period in 1996, a spokesman from the area's merchants association said Friday.

Exports from the largest free-trade zone in the Western Hemisphere, located in Colon 50 miles (80 km) from Panama City, were $1.38 billion from January to March, up from $1.31 billion during the same period in 1996, he said.
Imports, primarily from Asia, dipped 1.2 percent to $1.06 billion in the same period, down from $1.07 billion last year.
He stressed that "the free trade zone is recuperating from the import tax crisis we had last year."

Congress abolished last year a 15 percent tax on foreign sales after the area's 1,500 merchants staged work stoppages to protest the measure. They said the tax, which required them to make advance payments based on estimated earnings, hurt their trade. The tax had generated $30 million in revenues.
